nodes.bodyText:
Walkthrough



The change adds a shared board-theme rendering module. It resolves theme tokens and accessibility overrides, verifies content-addressed assets, and renders board cards as HTML or terminal text.
Changes: Board theme rendering

Summary




Theme contracts and public API  pkgs/id/src/boards/render.rs, pkgs/id/src/boards.rs, doc/2026-11-23T21-40-00Z_feature_board_theme_rendering/...
Defines reserved token roles, value validation, defaults, accessibility inputs, and resolved-theme types. Exposes the render module. The plan document describes scope and lists schema and client-wiring follow-ups.


Theme resolution and validation  pkgs/id/src/boards/render.rs
Resolves board and standalone post themes using the configured precedence and foreign-theme mode. Applies contrast and accessibility adjustments, and reports invalid or unavailable values. Tests cover cascade and accessibility behavior.


Asset verification and renderers  pkgs/id/src/boards/render.rs
Verifies asset hashes and supported formats. Adds HTML escaping and terminal sanitization, then renders board cards according to the resolved layout. Tests cover asset handling, layouts, and hostile input.

Issue 5680: This change implements theme precedence and accessibility overrides for rendering. It does not cover sharing flows, playable posts, or moderation.
Issue 5525: This change implements the portable theme rendering slice. Playable posts and other board-v1 work remain outside its scope.

The changeset adds render.rs with cascade resolution, asset verification, and HTML and terminal emitters, which matches the title. The title uses an issue-style reference (#6163), but the PR objectives cite PR #13806 and the title's number does not match that PR, which is a minor inconsistency and does not make the title misleading. Second, pkgs/id/src/boards.rs adds the private render module and its re-export, which connects the new module to the boards package. Third, a planning document under doc/ describes the same slice. Alternatively, reduce #6163 scope in the issue to the shared render layer and open a separate issue for client wiring.

code.title: feat(idp-provider): reference consumer + per-app integration pattern (#13416)

nodes.bodyText:
Caution
Review failed

The pull request is closed.





Walkthrough



The IdP provider package adds a public token verifier and a reference Axum consumer with authenticated read and role-gated write routes. It also adds an executable example, integration guidance, and tests for valid and invalid consumer requests.
Changes: Consumer token verification



Layer / File(s)
Summary




JWKS loading and access-token verification  pkgs/idp-provider/src/lib.rs, pkgs/idp-provider/src/verify.rs
The package exposes the verifier module and makes Jwk and Jwks deserializable. The verifier loads discovery data and JWKS, then checks token structure, signature, issuer, token use, and expiry.


Role-gated routes and example  pkgs/idp-provider/src/verify.rs, pkgs/idp-provider/examples/role-gated-app.rs, pkgs/idp-provider/README.md
The reference app adds /healthz, /read, and /write. Read requires a valid bearer token; write also requires the owner or orchestrator role. The example and README describe consumer setup and behavior.


Consumer authorization tests  pkgs/idp-provider/tests/consumer.rs
Integration tests cover provider-issued owner tokens, read-only tokens, ID tokens, expired and malformed tokens, and requests without a token.




Estimated code review effort: 3 (Moderate) | ~25 minutes

Change: Feature

Sequence Diagram(s)

  
    
      sequenceDiagram
  participant ConsumerApp
  participant OpenIDDiscovery
  participant JWKS
  participant Caller
  participant TokenVerifier
  ConsumerApp->>OpenIDDiscovery: Fetch OpenID configuration
  OpenIDDiscovery-->>ConsumerApp: Return jwks_uri
  ConsumerApp->>JWKS: Fetch keys
  JWKS-->>ConsumerApp: Return JWKS
  Caller->>ConsumerApp: Send request with bearer token
  ConsumerApp->>TokenVerifier: Verify access token
  TokenVerifier-->>ConsumerApp: Return verified claims or error

    
  
  
    
  
    
    
    Loading

  


Possibly related issues

13798 — The issue describes a PM-stack consumer using discovery, JWKS verification, and role-gated writes. This PR adds the reference consumer pattern, but not the separate aggregator integration.
9077 — The issue calls for a provider whose fleet consumers enforce roles server-side. This PR adds the consumer-side role gate, but not the provider login doors or account linking.

The GitHub comments collector now validates explicit and enumerated repository targets against an owner allowlist and repository-name rules. It also checks returned issue and review rows for canonical repository URLs that match the requested repository.

code.title: feat(pm-dispatch): guard pool-backed session launches

nodes.bodyText:
No actionable comments were generated in the recent review.



Walkthrough



The change packages placement-record, adds placement-guard configuration and account lookup, and applies placement checks before session creation for supported model routes. The guard validates the helper result and can select the model used to create the session.
Changes: Session placement guard



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Package and guard configuration  pkgs/fleet/placement/package.nix, pkgs/pm-dispatch/package.nix, pm-stack/dispatch/src/config.ts, pm-stack/dispatch/test/config.test.ts
Adds the fleet-placement-record package and makes it available to the pm-dispatch wrapper. Adds guard settings, environment overrides, and configuration tests.


Account resolution and placement enforcement  pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts, pm-stack/dispatch/src/placement-guard.ts, pm-stack/dispatch/test/opencode.test.ts, pm-stack/dispatch/test/placement-guard.test.ts
Adds active OpenCode credential-label lookup and placement mappings for supported OpenCode Go/Zen and ClinePass models. The guard runs placement-record, checks its result, and returns the selected pool and session model. Tests cover credential lookup, guard outcomes, and unsupported or disabled cases.


Session launch integration  pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts, pm-stack/dispatch/README.md
Runs the placement check before worktree or session creation, logs a returned placement, and uses its selected model for session creation. The documentation describes the covered routes and refusal path.




Estimated code review effort: 3 (Moderate) | ~25 minutes


Change: Feature

Sequence Diagram(s)

  
    
      sequenceDiagram
  participant DispatchServer
  participant OpenCodeClient
  participant PlacementGuard
  participant placement-record
  participant SessionCreator
  DispatchServer->>OpenCodeClient: fetch active credential label when required
  DispatchServer->>PlacementGuard: check requested model and launch details
  PlacementGuard->>placement-record: run placement check with policy, quota, pool, and task input
  placement-record-->>PlacementGuard: return placement record or refusal
  PlacementGuard-->>DispatchServer: return selected pool and session model
  DispatchServer->>SessionCreator: create session with selected model

    
  
  
    
  
    
    
    Loading

Closing as superseded — collision record.
This PR duplicates work that had already landed. Lane WQ claimed #13289 first (2026-11-23T12:56:56Z, comment 7101845383) and merged the same fix via PR #13356 (c83e4410241); the issue is closed as completed. Cause of the duplicate, stated plainly: my pre-claim ownership read used gh api --paginate ... --jq with an object-shaped jq expression and stderr discarded, so the read errored (expected an object but got: array) and presented as an empty comment thread. The claim check therefore false-cleared. The implementation here was built and verified independently (64/64 hosted tests, mutation-checked), but it is the same change in substance and lands nothing.
Process lesson recorded for the lane briefs: paginated list reads need the .[] jq shape, and an ownership read must never suppress stderr — an errored read is not an empty thread.

Walkthrough



The browser can select kitty key encoding with ?keyboard=kitty. SSH serving adds default-off kitty negotiation, gated by the startup probe and explicit opt-in. Engaged SSH input is assembled into key tokens; unsupported or unverified sessions retain legacy input handling.
Changes: Kitty Keyboard Support



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Browser encoder selection  pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts, pkgs/id/web/src/world-keyboard.ts, pkgs/id/web/src/world-keyboard-optin.test.ts
The page selects the rich encoder when keyboard=kitty and the legacy encoder otherwise. Tests check encoded key input, shortcut handling, and paste frames.


Kitty keyboard state and framing  pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh/kitty.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/input_framing.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/lib.rs, pkgs/id/src/lib.rs
The kitty state machine verifies reports, queues assembled tokens, and supports fallback. The input framing module is exposed through the crates.


SSH opt-in and probe outcome  pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/src/commands/serve.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh/form_io.rs
SSH options carry the default-off setting through serving to shells. Probe expiry retains the probe outcome for the shell.


SSH negotiation and input routing  pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs, doc/2026-11-02T_reference_kitty_disambiguate_v1.md
The shell gates negotiation on opt-in and probe support, frames input while engaged, and restores its owned profile. Tests cover negotiation, fallback, and legacy behavior. The reference describes the implementation and activation conditions.

Evidence update — the gate is not met: the branch's test target does not compile
1. The remote executor cannot produce this evidence (defect filed)
The settling command is cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh from pkgs/id (the world_ssh module is behind the ssh feature; without it the new code compiles out, so the earlier 969-green run proved nothing). Two fleet-command runs — 45249821636 and 45255497015 — failed identically before any test ran:
error: failed to run custom build command for ring v0.17.14
could not execute process …/build-script-build (never executed)
No such file or directory (os error 2)

Deterministic, not a flake: the ring build-script binary cannot execute in the baked executor image (aws-lc-sys is in the same tree). Filed as dezren39/fleet#111 — any crate with a native build-script dependency of this class is unbuildable in the executor until it is fixed.
2. Venue moved to the laptop
Per the remote-builds rule's own fallback (a job that cannot be dispatched successfully falls back, with the reason recorded — this is that record), the suite was run on amd-6 in a fresh worktree of origin/felix/787-kitty-slice-e-f (head 00520a8a3), same command: cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh from pkgs/id.
3. Result: compile failure in this PR's own test code — no tests ran
error: could not compile id-worlds (lib test) due to 9 previous errors. All 9 are in the #[cfg(test)] code of crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs:

E0428 (world_ssh.rs:3269): read_until_bytes is defined twice in the test module — an older 4-argument version at line 3059 (channel, terminal: &mut vt100::Parser, needle: &str, …) and a newer 3-argument version at line 3269 (channel, needle: &[u8], timeout: Duration).
E0061 (world_ssh.rs:3943): a test calls serve_limited(...) with 5 arguments; the function now takes 6 — the missing argument is this PR's own new SshServeOptions.
E0308 ×7 (world_ssh.rs:3328, 3335, 3401, 3403, 3410, 3451, 3495): test calls written against the newer read_until_bytes signature resolve to the older definition and mismatch.

No errors are in kitty.rs itself, but the kitty unit tests live in the same lib test target, so zero tests executed — the six kitty tests and the world_ssh:: tests have still never run anywhere: remote runs without ssh compiled the module out, and remote runs with ssh died at ring before reaching this code.
What is needed
Reconcile the two generations of test helpers in world_ssh.rs (one read_until_bytes; update the serve_limited call with the options argument), then re-run the same command. The full laptop log is on amd-6 at /home/user/787-kitty-evidence.log. This PR is not merged on this evidence.

Fix lane update (felix): the test target compiles again; one runtime failure remains, and it is a production trigger defect, not a test defect — not fixed here, diagnosis below.
The compile fix — commit c15154708
Test code only, in pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs (+11/−5), no assertions changed:

The screen-based helper (channel, &mut vt100::Parser, &str needle; panics on timeout) is renamed read_until_screen_bytes, with its four call sites updated (the read_until wrapper and the repaint test, whose waits are on rendered screen contents).
read_until_bytes is now only the raw-byte form (channel, &[u8] needle, timeout) the kitty tests are written against; its seven call sites resolve to it. The E0428 duplicate and the seven E0308s are gone.
The TwoTransports fixture's serve_limited call now passes SshServeOptions::default() (the E0061), matching start_limited.

Evidence — laptop (amd-6), worktree at pushed head c15154708
The remote executor still cannot build this tree (dezren39/fleet#111), so the run stayed on the laptop, under fleet-build-lock:
cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh from pkgs/id — 1025 passed / 1 failed (28.16s).

The six kitty unit tests, all ok: flags_reports_parse_only_the_exact_shape, the_filter_consumes_only_the_outstanding_answer, verification_flips_active_only_on_the_disambiguate_flag, keys_coalesced_with_the_answer_keep_their_order, fallback_keeps_held_token_bytes_and_the_owed_pop, split_tokens_complete_across_feeds.
world_ssh:: tests: 57 executed, 56 ok. Kitty integration: kitty_stays_off_without_the_server_opt_in ok, kitty_stays_off_when_the_terminal_reports_no_support ok, kitty_opt_in_falls_back_when_the_push_does_not_take ok, kitty_opt_in_negotiates_verifies_and_frames_split_input FAILED.

The remaining failure — production activation trigger
kitty_opt_in_negotiates_verifies_and_frames_split_input fails deterministically (3/3 isolated re-runs, ~10.1s each) at the "one push + verify burst after detection" assertion: expected 1, got 0. A diagnostic run (assert message patched on the laptop only, since reverted) shows the read buffer is empty — after the terminal answers the probe with CSI ? 0 u, the server sends nothing at all for the full 10s window. Not a chunking/contiguity issue: the burst is never written until further input arrives.
Root cause, in the raw-mode input path of world_ssh.rs: maybe_begin_kitty() is invoked only at the top of the inbound-receive routine. That routine's probe-wait loop closes the probe on its 250 ms deadline, and when no held bytes remain it loops into a bare frames.recv() park — it does not re-check activation. So once the probe closes with detected support, the push waits until one more input frame arrives and is returned as legacy input, and only the next receive call attempts activation. The sibling fallback test passes precisely because it sends another key (q), which prods the loop into activating; this test sends nothing after the probe answer, per the design contract that negotiation follows detection.
That is production logic (when activation is attempted), so per lane discipline it is reported, not rewritten here. Suggested shape for the fix, for whoever picks it up: after close_terminal_probe() in the probe-wait loop, loop back through the activation check instead of parking on frames.recv() — i.e. re-run maybe_begin_kitty() before waiting for more input. The test stands as written; it states the design's contract.

Production fix landed — head 0b344c9d2 (on top of c15154708). The suite is now fully green with the previously failing test passing.
The change — one file, pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs, SshIo::recv, Raw mode (+18 lines, no test touched, no assertion changed): in the probe-wait loop's deadline arm, after close_terminal_probe() returns no held bytes, the loop now runs the same activation check the top of recv() runs — maybe_begin_kitty().await, and if the kitty engine is engaged, returns kitty_next() mapped the same way (token / resize / closed) — instead of looping into the bare frames.recv() park. When the probe closes without support or without the opt-in, kitty_may_activate() is false, the check is a no-op, and the loop parks exactly as before, so the legacy and fallback paths are unchanged. Cancel-safety is preserved: the probe is already taken by close_terminal_probe() at that point, and no new await is introduced across the demux.
This matches the diagnosis in the previous comment: the burst (push + verify) was only ever attempted at the top of the next recv() call, so a terminal that answered the probe and then waited for the push stalled until the user typed again — the extra key in the fallback test was what prodded it into activating.
Evidence — laptop (amd-6), worktree reset to the pushed head 0b344c9d2, under fleet-build-lock (the remote executor still cannot build this tree — dezren39/fleet#111): cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh from pkgs/id:

1026 passed / 0 failed (27.86s), exit 0. Full log on amd-6 at /home/user/787-kitty-fix-evidence.log.
world_ssh::tests::kitty_opt_in_negotiates_verifies_and_frames_split_input — ok (previously failing deterministically: expected 1 push+verify burst, got 0).
Siblings still ok: kitty_opt_in_falls_back_when_the_push_does_not_take, kitty_stays_off_without_the_server_opt_in, kitty_stays_off_when_the_terminal_reports_no_support.
All six kitty unit tests ok: flags_reports_parse_only_the_exact_shape, the_filter_consumes_only_the_outstanding_answer, verification_flips_active_only_on_the_disambiguate_flag, keys_coalesced_with_the_answer_keep_their_order, fallback_keeps_held_token_bytes_and_the_owed_pop, split_tokens_complete_across_feeds.

No new dependencies. Ready for Felix's merge.

Verifying this PR at b44c08e0b59 for the #13237 follow-on, I confirmed the Codex P2 first-hand: grant/revoke built their audit event via record_event but never appended it to RoleRegistry.events, so events() omitted every grant, revocation, and refusal — against the module's own contract. The existing audit test passed because it only asserted the returned outcome events.
Fix commit f404907bad2 (one file, +27/−4): record_event now appends the event it builds, and grant_list_revoke_are_audited additionally asserts the full events() sequence (create, refused grant, grant, refused re-grant, revoke, refused revoke, two grants). Evidence: role_config suite 4/4 green at the new head; mutation check — the strengthened test fails with the append removed. Full cargo test -p id-caps at the original head was 253/253 unit + 13/3/1 integration green; the full suite is being re-run at f404907bad2 before merge.

Shepherd update (Lane WP) — verified green, but NOT mergeable: blocked on a design conflict with #13202, recorded on #8299.
Verification (all first-hand): full cargo test -p id-caps green at b44c08e0b59 (253 unit + 13 + 3 + 1 integration) and again at f404907bad2 with the audit-log fix. The Codex P2 is fixed in f404907bad2 (see the shepherd note above).
The merge itself fails: this branch modifies pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/agent_policy.rs, which PR #13202 (commit 576950cd81a) deleted on main, reconciling the two #7916 policy points into mcp_policy::PolicySession. Concretely:

role_config.rs imports crate::agent_policy::Quota. On main, Quota lives in crate::mcp_policy and already derives Deserialize — that part ports trivially.
The blocker is PolicyPoint::refresh_ceiling and its acceptance test ceiling_refresh_applies_next_frame. mcp_policy documents the opposite position, in CapabilityCeiling's own doc: "The ceiling can only be changed owner-side, out-of-band — a session holds the grant it was constructed with." Porting refresh_ceiling onto PolicySession would reverse a design decision the reconciliation just landed; reinterpreting the acceptance as owner-side re-grant is a different change than this PR makes. That call belongs to #8299's owner, not a shepherd — the options are laid out on #8299.

State left: PR head f404907bad2 (original commit + the audit fix), branch otherwise untouched, no merge attempted against the conflicting base. Once the #8299 decision lands, the rebase is small: move the Quota import, and either port or drop the refresh slice per the decision.

Took the shepherd from Lane WP's decision-needed note (13:23Z). Decision recorded on #8299: option 1 — refresh wins (owner-side ceiling-refresh on mcp_policy::PolicySession; reasoning on the issue). Execution is parked: fetching this PR's head ref tripped a platform execution-risk check on the branch content, so per the standing rule for this flag class I ran no git/build/test operations on it and deleted the fetched ref. Walkthrough



The PR adds a public host-side policy point for delegated agent actions. It checks action ceilings, delegation expiry, revisions, rate limits, and quotas; charges admitted actions; parks sessions on quota exhaustion; and records signed, verifiable audit events.
Changes: Agent policy point



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Session admission and action checks  pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/agent_policy.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/lib.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/tests/agent_policy_point.rs
The crate exposes the policy module and adds grant-derived ceilings and action admission checks. Tests cover refusals for ceiling violations, stale revisions, expired delegations, rate limits, and unlisted programs, as well as object-class checks.


Quota exhaustion and parking  pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/agent_policy.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/tests/agent_policy_point.rs
The policy point charges admitted actions against quota and parks a session when an action exceeds its budget. Tests check pre-execution charging and subsequent parked-session refusals.


Audit verification and owner summaries  pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/agent_policy.rs, pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/tests/agent_policy_point.rs
The policy point records actions in a signed audit chain and provides owner summaries. Tests check join and action events, chain verification and tamper detection, summary contents, and a mixed-action sequence.




Estimated code review effort: 4 (Complex) | ~60 minutes


Change: Feature

Sequence Diagram(s)

  
    
      sequenceDiagram
  participant Caller
  participant PolicyPoint
  participant Ceiling
  participant AuditLog
  Caller->>PolicyPoint: admit(action, revision, now)
  PolicyPoint->>Ceiling: check(action)
  Ceiling-->>PolicyPoint: allow or refusal
  PolicyPoint->>AuditLog: record signed action event
  PolicyPoint-->>Caller: return Admission

    
  
  
    
  
    
    
    Loading

  


Possibly related issues

#7916: The PR implements the policy point, capability ceiling, per-session quota, parking, and audit log described as the spike’s work items.
#6280: The PR implements a policy point covering capability ceilings, per-action quotas, and audit records, which are topics in this issue.
#8302: The PR provides refusal audit records and an OwnerSummary; the issue also requires a review view and one-shot approval, which this PR does not add.

Suggested reviewers: claude





Merge Risk:  Moderate · up to bb2d2






This adds a new host-side policy layer for agent actions, but it does not yet enforce several of the guarantees it describes. A session can be opened with tools that the verified grant does not allow, and a bare program-invoke action bypasses the program allowlist. The audit log can also record actions as executed before they run, or become unverifiable if the signing key changes mid-session. No production code uses the module yet, so nothing is broken today, but these gaps should be closed before hosts start relying on it.

The change adds shared metadata checks, a GitHub webhook route, and a command-line sweeper. Both ingestion paths process issues and pull requests, store non-triage outcomes, write generated metadata when configured, and forward triage outcomes.

Layer / File(s)
Summary




Metadata checks and outcomes  pm-stack/aggregator/src/metadata-ingestion.ts, pm-stack/aggregator/test/metadata-ingestion.test.ts
The shared module parses metadata blocks, resolves parents, and returns current, generated, or triage outcomes. It builds triage packets and stores non-triage records. Tests cover parsing, parent resolution, outcomes, persistence, and packet fields.


GitHub webhook processing  pm-stack/aggregator/src/webhook-listener.ts, pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts, pm-stack/aggregator/test/webhook-listener.test.ts, pm-stack/aggregator/test/nav.test.ts
The webhook handler validates signed requests and processes supported issue and pull-request events. The server wires epic lookup, metadata write-back, and triage enqueueing. Tests cover generated outcomes, triage, invalid signatures, and ignored events.


Repository sweep and CLI  pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/metadata-sweeper.ts
The CLI validates options, fetches issues and pull requests, and runs metadata checks. It supports dry runs, optional queue forwarding, generated body updates, and error reporting.

Shepherd fix-forward (Lane WT, archer) — commit 1e4e5ac9e39 on this branch addresses both P2 findings from the Codex review of eba7c271538:

Permission forwarded to spawned servers. augmentAdapters now puts MCPX_ADAPTERS_ALLOW_BARE=true into the spawned adapter serve child's environment whenever the daemon's resolved adapters.allowBare is on. The child re-resolves its own settings, so a grant made only by the daemon's --adapters-allow-bare flag was invisible there and the child refused the declaration its parent accepted. The variable is declared in settings.ScriptEnv (with docs/environment.md regenerated), as the ScriptEnv contract requires for anything mcpx writes into a child's environment.
Live add refuses before persisting. handleAdaptersAdd now applies the gate to the submitted spec before config.AddAdapterEntry: a bare declaration posted while the setting is off gets a 400 naming the setting, and nothing is written — instead of a 500 at reload with the poisoned declaration left on disk. The gate itself moved to adapter.CheckBareAllowed, shared by the CLI load path, the serve path, and the daemon add, with one error text.

New tests: TestAugmentAdaptersForwardsAllowBareToTheChild (cli), TestAdapterAddRefusesBareWhileAllowBareOff / TestAdapterAddAcceptsBareWhenAllowBareOn (daemon); the existing gate unit test now calls the shared function.
Verification (laptop route): internal/adapter, internal/settings, internal/cli (full, 33s), internal/daemon (full, 184s), examples, internal/execsvc, internal/sdnotify all pass at 1e4e5ac9e39; the e2e allowBare gate probe and effect-probe test pass. Closed at review — wrong direction. Do not merge.
Review finding (felix): the proposal's change contradicts its own evidence and its own expected-effect statement.

The code: a pool reads "near" when windowPercent(w) >= NEAR_PCT (derive.ts:174). Raising NEAR_PCT 85 → 90 therefore moves caution entry from 85% to 90% — LATER, with less headroom — and narrows the caution band [NEAR_PCT, 100).
The evidence: weekly walls arrive systematically EARLY (positive median signed wall error = projected wall time later than the realized wall: meta +4,741 min, anthropic:claude-pro +795 min). The correct response is caution EARLIER, i.e. NEAR_PCT down (85 → 80), widening the band.
The proposal's expected effect — "the fraction of realized weekly walls preceded by a tick with the pool in the caution state rises" — would be served by lowering the threshold and is undermined by raising it.

The generator conflated "widen the margin of safety" with "raise the number". The machinery (evidence gates, refusal path, PR-only allowlist) is unaffected; the defect is local to the caution-margin class's step direction. A fix is being dispatched against #12700: the step direction must derive from the sign of the grounding pools' median signed wall error (early walls ⇒ threshold down; late walls ⇒ threshold up), pinned by tests, and the generator re-run — if the evidence still grounds a margin step, the corrected proposal (85 → 80) will be filed as a new PR for disposition.

Closing as superseded — the F12.11 phase 3 work landed through two other PRs, and this branch's implementation should not be merged:

Rust slice: #12655 (merged 2026-11-22T18:49Z) — negotiated binary v2 ScreenPatch transport: screen_msgpack join flag, ViewPatchFrame MessagePack envelope in id-core on the #12241 codec, NUL-marker framing on the length-prefixed transports, native binary WebSocket messages, shell contract revision 12, with session/net/ssh/ws test evidence recorded on the PR.
Browser/TS slice: #12667 — strict TS decoder at golden-vector parity with the merged Rust codec, join offer, binary patch application with the JSON path's fallback discipline; test-web-unit 879 passed / 0 failed.

Why not this PR: its codec is a flat envelope that replaces the merged #12241 codec and its golden vectors; its framed transports carry no kind/marker byte and its Rust client cannot consume its own v2 frames; its final head (3751be8) was never test-run (its own body notes this). Its design note's join-opt-in argument was adopted in substance — the merged design gates binary on the join's screen_msgpack flag plus screen_patches plus a byte-capable transport.
Disposition of the review findings on this PR:

The four Codex P2s on pkgs/fleet/... files (shell.rs build lock ×2, next.rs pagination/handout ×2): those files left this PR's diff in its rebase; stale, unrelated to #12242, not actioned here.
Browser clears its rendered baseline on reconnect while keeping the resume token (world.ts): addressed in this PR's later commits, but the behavior area is superseded; the underlying v1 resume behavior is unchanged by either landing PR.
Host does not restore the session viewport from the retained baseline on resume (world.ts): filed as follow-up #12648, which names this PR's approach (head 3751be8) as the starting point and notes its regression test was never run and must be executed, not just ported.

Thanks to the author for the early design work — the negotiation question it opened (explicit opt-in vs endpoint-only) is settled in the merged contract's offer-and-observe rule.

Evidence (shepherd pass, queue task 17244):

This PR implements the #7358 decision recorded 2026-11-10: claim/list/health must resolve a queue (--queue, else REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE) or die(2). The next day the one-queue broker model (#8097, PR #8438, deployed 2026-11-11) deliberately replaced claim semantics, and current main's client.rs documents the settled rule in opt_queue_claim: "an explicit --queue wins, then the REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE env; with neither, the claim is UNSCOPED (None) and the broker claims across the one fleet queue in priority order. Every other command keeps opt_queue's built-in default."
Landing this PR would make unscoped fleet queue claim exit 2 — but unscoped claiming is exactly how all twelve repo-queue lanes now work by design (per-repo queue names are stream labels inside the one queue, not separate queues). The shadow-default trap the PR guards against was dissolved by that redesign: claim no longer resolves through DEFAULT_QUEUE at all.
The two CodeRabbit findings (smoke.sh coverage of the new failure mode; queue-specific empty-health message) are moot on a branch that must not land.
Left open on purpose: #7358's list/health leg. On current main, list/health still resolve via opt_queue → default_queue() (env, else the built-in shadow name) — whether that should tighten is a fresh, scoped decision for the issue owner in the one-queue world, not something to smuggle in on this pre-redesign branch. The finding (valid): review rows written before this PR's submitted_at switch carry a fabricated delivery-time source_updated_at later than their true submitted_at; the monotonic upsert guard in pm-stack/projector/src/store.ts would then refuse every later new-rule webhook for those reviews, freezing the rows (dismissals etc. would never land).
The fix: upsertComment's guard now also admits exactly the correcting update — same review (equal submitted_at), existing row still fabricated (source_updated_at > submitted_at), incoming row following the new rule (source_updated_at = its submitted_at). The correction is one-time and self-limiting: once it lands the row is self-consistent, the branch can never fire for it again, and ordinary monotonicity resumes. No backfill job is needed; each legacy row heals on its next webhook, and rows that never receive another webhook keep their (immutable) review content with only the timestamp provenance the PR already documents.
Tests: three new regression tests in test/store.test.ts pin (1) the correction lands and updates review_state, (2) monotonicity resumes afterward (a stale replay is refused), (3) the branch never fires for non-review rows. Full projector suite locally: 119 tests, 0 failures.

nodes.bodyText:

The session inbox now records whether a command has started. Recovery runs commands without a recorded start, skips commands whose row is gone, and reports previously started commands as interrupted rather than rerunning them.

Summary




Persist and claim command starts  packages/core/src/session/sql.ts, packages/core/src/database/migration/20261123232422_session_inbox_started.ts, packages/core/src/database/migration.gen.ts, packages/core/src/database/schema.gen.ts, packages/core/schema.json, packages/core/src/session/inbox.ts

Walkthrough



The changes add session-specific model-pool pins with failover, expose pin management through session APIs, extend client API contracts, and adjust HTTP API code generation to ignore opaque schema filters.
Changes: Session route pins



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Pool pin storage and selection  packages/core/src/model-route.ts, packages/core/test/model-route-pin.test.ts
Model routes store bounded in-memory pins and prioritize a pinned leaf when it is ready, untried, and gate-open. Tests cover selection modes, nested pools, pin storage, and failover order.


Resolver pin preference  packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts, packages/core/test/model-resolver.test.ts
The resolver supplies a session pin as the preferred target when it is ready and not quota-demoted. Tests cover health changes, pool membership, user overrides, and session isolation.


Session route-target API  packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts, packages/core/src/session.ts, packages/core/src/session/error.ts, packages/core/src/session/route-target.ts, packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts, packages/client/src/effect/api/api.ts, packages/server/test/route-target.test.ts
Session routes can list, set, and clear pins. Setting a pin checks the route and pool membership; removing a session clears its pins. Server tests cover valid updates, invalid targets, and missing sessions.



Client API contracts



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Client API operations and event shapes  packages/client/src/effect/api/api.ts, packages/client/test/promise.test.ts
Client types add server redemption, transcriptions, and route-override operations. Session event data gains optional provider and model fields on error events and optional plan notices on step-ended events.



Code generation filter normalization



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Normalize opaque schema filters  packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts, packages/httpapi-codegen/test/generate.test.ts
Code generation strips filters without a code representation from string and number ASTs. The regression test checks the emitted Effect shape and Promise types.

Per-session model-pool pins work with failover and return to the pinned member. A pin to a variant-less model reference can select a later variant-less duplicate instead of the first match. The preference stays within the configured pool and retains existing eligibility and failover controls. The inspected change establishes no material weakening of security, failure containment, rollback, or ownership guarantees.
Retained concerns
No architecture-level concerns identified.

Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — The new routing authority is a preference among a session's current pool members, not an arbitrary provider destination or credential input. Pin state is keyed by session and route, and the inspected mutation does not change credentials, permissions, or the session's selected pool.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — Both handlers require an existing session. The write endpoint additionally uses session-location middleware; its validation location comes from the stored session rather than the submitted target. The read endpoint omits location initialization and returns stored preferences after the same session-existence check. Both are registered through the existing API authorization layer.
observed — The code-generation change removes unrenderable custom string and number filters from copied generation ASTs. It does not replace the server endpoint schemas; the inspected change therefore does not remove server-side request validation.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

observed — The preference is withheld during last-resort selection when nothing is ready. Avoid overrides, applicable budgets, cooldowns, credential and provider quota gates, request ceilings, and tree gates remain upstream checks rather than being bypassed by a pin.

The route planner now tracks consecutive authentication refusals across a provider’s models. At three refusals, it gates the provider and its root starts using an escalating cooldown. A successful completion or resetHealth clears the provider’s hard-failure record.

The route planner counts consecutive provider authentication refusals. From the third refusal, it applies a cooldown that can extend with further refusals, up to the configured maximum. The active gate contributes to provider cooldown checks and blocks root starts even when the quota root-start switch is off.


Clear provider gate and validate behavior  packages/core/src/model-route.ts, packages/core/test/model-route.test.ts
A completed request and resetHealth clear provider hard-failure state. Tests cover provider-wide gating, cooldown extension, clearing after success, health events, and an ordinary failure between authentication refusals.

The new gate is meant to stop repeated attempts against a provider with failing credentials. It can still let attempts through after its timer lapses, after a later refusal shortens it, or via subsession fallback. Address these before merging, or explicitly accept them as a deviation from the issue's acceptance criteria.





Security architecture risk:  Moderate · up to 12c1c





A single failing credential can temporarily block new sessions from using otherwise healthy credentials or models of the same provider. Expiry and successful requests provide recovery, but the change weakens failure isolation between credentials.
Retained concerns

Medium · reliability · inferred: The new counter treats three authentication refusals from any credential or model as provider-wide failure evidence. Refusals from one invalid credential, including already-concurrent attempts, can therefore exclude healthy sibling credentials and unrelated models from new root sessions. The base kept these refusals credential-and-traffic scoped. Once gated, newly starting sessions cannot supply the healthy success that would clear the record early; recovery depends on expiry or another already-admitted request succeeding. This broadens a credential-local fault into a provider-wide availability failure within the process.

Security Findings and Attack Paths

inferred — The supported adverse path is authentication-failure amplification: three qualifying refusals associated with one credential can affect healthy access elsewhere under the provider ID. Upstream error metadata and response text supply the classification. This trace does not establish that an ordinary prompt author can manufacture those errors or that the effect crosses a tenant boundary.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — The change uses authentication responses as scheduling evidence, not as permission to access the provider. Existing policy and context-overflow exclusions remain in the runner. Success clearing requires a successfully finished stream without recorded provider failure and with observed output.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

observed — Containment and recovery are bounded rather than absolute. The provider record expires, any provider success clears it, and health reset removes it. Existing target probes can bypass ordinary cooldown exclusion, and non-root last-resort selection can admit cooling targets; new root starts still undergo the explicit provider gate.

Hardening Proposals

proposed — Preserve credential-level failure isolation unless provider-wide failure is corroborated across eligible credential identities or established by an explicitly provider-global signal. A healthy sibling credential should retain a bounded opportunity to demonstrate recovery before all new root sessions are excluded.

The baseline also waited indefinitely on that body; this PR reduces its buffering but does not introduce or worsen the stall exposure.

Walkthrough



The transcription route now derives a request-body limit from enabled provider registrations. It rejects oversized declared or streamed bodies with HTTP 413 and collects streamed bodies that remain within the limit.

Layer / File(s)
Summary




Registration-based body limits  packages/core/src/transcription-facade.ts, packages/core/test/transcription-facade.test.ts
The façade adds a 64 KiB multipart allowance and calculates limits per registration and across registrations. Tests cover the largest limit, provider filtering, and the empty-provider fallback.


Bounded route body reading  packages/server/src/handlers/transcriptions.ts, packages/server/test/transcriptions.test.ts, script/check-bounded-http.allowlist.txt
The route loads enabled providers before reading the body. It returns 413 when a declared or streamed body exceeds the limit. Tests cover oversized bodies, a stream that remains open, and an under-limit request reaching provider gating. The allowlist now describes the bounded streamed read.




Estimated code review effort: 3 (Moderate) | ~20 minutes


Change: Bug fix · Severity of issue fixed: Medium

Sequence Diagram(s)

  
    
      sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant transcriptionRoute
  participant EnabledProviderCatalog
  participant TranscriptionFacade
  Client->>transcriptionRoute: Send multipart request
  transcriptionRoute->>EnabledProviderCatalog: Load enabled providers
  EnabledProviderCatalog-->>transcriptionRoute: Return enabled provider set
  transcriptionRoute->>TranscriptionFacade: Calculate maximum body limit
  TranscriptionFacade-->>transcriptionRoute: Return body limit
  Client->>transcriptionRoute: Stream request body
  transcriptionRoute-->>Client: Return 413 audio_too_large when limit is exceeded

Merge Risk:  Minimal · up to e1186






Oversized transcription uploads are now rejected with 413 while the body is being read, and valid uploads and invalid-audio errors behave as before. No concrete merge-blocking risk remains.





Security architecture risk:  Minimal · up to e1186





The change rejects oversized uploads earlier and preserves the exact per-model file limit. No introduced material security regression was established in the inspected flow.

No architecture-level concerns identified.

Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — A caller able to submit transcription requests controls body bytes, declared length and multipart fields. The principal affected asset is serving-process memory and availability. The new control applies per request; it does not establish an aggregate concurrency limit or a strict process-memory ceiling, because transport chunks and subsequent parsing copies also consume memory. Internet exposure and tenant boundaries were not established.

Security Findings and Attack Paths

inferred — The inspected oversized-upload path is interrupted earlier than at base: actual bytes are counted independently of Content-Length, and an exceeded ceiling returns before multipart parsing or credential-bearing provider dispatch. This supports an availability improvement, not a claim that all denial-of-service paths are eliminated.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — The whole-body ceiling supplements rather than replaces the exact registration cap. Model resolution filters by enabled providers, and the handler returns validation failures before invoking either facade method.
observed — Provider configuration is now captured before the upload read and reused afterward. Dispatch trusts the resolved registration and reads its configured environment credential without another catalog check. The PR therefore lengthens the snapshot-to-dispatch interval, although the required semantics for disabling a provider during an in-flight request are not established.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

observed — The handler bounds bytes but introduces no upload-duration timeout. An upload stalled below the ceiling can therefore remain pending at this layer, as the base full-body read could. Connection cancellation and unread-body cleanup depend on runtime behavior not verified here.

Hardening Proposals

proposed — If provider disable is intended to revoke uploads already in progress, retain the initial catalog snapshot for the read ceiling but refresh provider eligibility before final resolution or dispatch. This is conditional hardening, not an established violation of the current contract.

Retained concerns

Medium · security · inferred: Provider-only cookies still participate in the store's shared login-selection state. If older credential A is explicitly active and newer credential B is inactive, creating a cookie with the default activation behavior clears A's active flag. Connection projection then removes the cookie and selects B by recency. Thus storing a quota-only secret can change the effective login identity without selecting that login. The existing cookie test has only one login credential and therefore does not contradict this multi-credential case. Medium · reliability · inferred: A rollback to the comparison base cannot reuse a database containing session-cookie credentials transparently. The new version persists the new variant in the existing table, while the base decoder accepts only the three previous variants and synchronously decodes every returned row without isolating unsupported values. A retained cookie row therefore fails global credential listing and that integration's credential reads; filtering it from connections occurs too late. This is a conditional rollback incompatibility, not evidence of a deployed failure. A database-restoration or pre-downgrade cleanup procedure was not supplied.

inferred — The material security path is account-selection drift: cookie creation can clear the explicitly selected login, after which cookie filtering exposes a different stored login as active. nodes.bodyText:
Walkthrough



Claude credential renewal now rereads the shared credentials file before exchange attempts and after responses. It adopts changed refresh tokens, checks rejected tokens against stored state, and avoids replacing a newer credential with a late exchange result. Tests cover concurrent rotations and the bounded-adoption behavior.
Changes: Shared credential renewal



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Credential adoption and rejection handling  packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts, packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts
Renewal adopts a changed stored refresh token before an exchange and rechecks stored state after a rejected grant. Adoption is limited to three attempts. Tests cover rate limits, rejected grants, the adoption bound, and switching to a token that needs renewal.


Late exchange result guard  packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts, packages/ai/test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts
Renewal discards an exchange result if another writer has stored a different refresh token. Tests verify the newer stored credential remains unchanged.




Estimated code review effort: 3 (Moderate) | ~25 minutes


Change: Bug fix

Possibly related issues

#2467: Describes the same adoption-bound and rejected-grant paths. Its stated acceptance criteria concern behavior after the adoption limit.

Possibly related PRs

developing-today-forks/opencode#2270: Adds standing renewal retries for Claude Code credentials. Both PRs modify the renewal exchange path and share its behavior.






Merge Risk:  Moderate · up to ad356






Concurrent Claude credential loads can exchange the same single-use refresh token after adoption, potentially causing authentication failures. Transfer renewal ownership to the adopted token before merging.





Security architecture risk:  Moderate · up to ad356





The change reduces stale-token replay and credential overwrites. However, adopting a different refresh token does not transfer ownership of the active renewal. Overlapping requests can therefore exchange the same single-use token, risking rejection and disruption of the shared login.
Retained concerns

Medium · reliability · inferred: Adopting a renewal-due token does not transfer single-flight ownership. Renewal A remains registered under its original token after switching to stored token B. A concurrent request reading B passes the renewal-due check, finds neither an in-flight nor standing entry under B, and can exchange B alongside A. The post-exchange guard runs too late to prevent duplicate presentation of that single-use token. The base could replay stale tokens across writers, but did not switch a renewal to another token while retaining its original coordination key. This new ownership mismatch threatens shared-login continuity when the replacement credential is itself due and exchanges overlap.


Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — The affected asset is the OAuth login represented by one configured credentials file and the clients sharing that login. Duplicate single-use exchanges can cause grant rejection; the module additionally describes possible token-family revocation. Broader tenant or service compromise is not established by the inspected path.

Security Findings and Attack Paths

inferred — The identified failure requires a stored replacement that remains within the renewal window and overlapping renewal execution, not an authentication bypass. Legitimate concurrent loads can trigger it after another writer changes the file. A replacement outside that window is returned without exchange, providing strong counterevidence against a general failure on every adoption.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — The credential file remains a trusted source, as it was before this PR. Existing writes validate token fields, use a temporary file with mode 0600, rename it into place, and attempt temporary-file cleanup on failure. These controls protect against invalid blobs and partial replacement, but do not serialize renewal owners.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

inferred — The new rereads narrow existing stale-presentation and overwrite windows without making exchange and persistence atomic across processes. Another writer can still rotate after the pre-exchange read or after the post-exchange check. Those cross-process windows existed in the base and are residual architecture limitations, not additional introduced concerns.

Hardening Proposals

proposed — Keep in-process renewal ownership stable across token adoption, either by coordinating on credential-store identity or by atomically joining or claiming the adopted token's owner before exchange. Validate the request-versus-standing interleaving where both observe an already-due replacement token.

inferred — No introduced privilege-escalation path was established in the inspected changes. observed — The runner obtains parent identity from the loaded session record. The inspected creation service requires a referenced parent to exist, inherits its location, and applies model governance before publishing the child. These checks establish provenance within that service, not proof of external API authorization coverage.
observed — The new restriction is not universal execution enforcement. Initial direct-model resolution still loads the explicitly selected model before attaching any route fallback, and a runner resolution without a selected session model uses the context-free resolver path. These paths predate the PR; they should not be interpreted as newly introduced bypasses or as coverage by the root-start gate.

inferred — The principal introduced risk is rejection containment, not increased authority: the sticky-key mismatch can apply admission refusal to previously admitted work. Retained continuity and the independent disable flag limit that risk and provide a reversible operational escape.

Merge Risk:  Moderate · up to ad841






When the render tool is enabled, quota-fallback answers can be silently ignored: a later switch can lose to an earlier tier choice, or an offered switch or downgrade may not resolve to a model. The session then keeps using the walled model. Behavior without the render tool is unchanged. Fix both before merging.





Security architecture risk:  Moderate · up to ad841





Recovery choices can be recorded without being applied, leaving execution on the previous provider. Verification that answers changing shared preferences are user-authorized also depends on an external component.
Retained concerns

Medium · security · inferred: Completed render-tool output now acquires user authority without being bound to a particular outstanding card or its offered choices. A structurally valid tier/model answer can update the shared plan store, append a user-source note, and stage a session model change even when no chooser is outstanding. If the external host permits page-script-generated or stale submissions, those outputs can exercise this authority without an additional intent check. Host-side enforcement was unavailable, so attacker reachability remains inferred rather than a verified exploit.
Medium · reliability · observed: The quota card can offer switch and downgrade choices that the executor cannot resolve. The supplied test fixture has DeepSeek only at cheap and Anthropic at standard/frontier, yet its card offers DeepSeek/standard and Anthropic/cheap. After either choice, the wall is cleared and the answer recorded, but the next step removes the pending action before looking up its model. A missing model silently leaves the previous selection active, defeating the selected recovery path and allowing another request against the exhausted provider instead of containing the failure or reporting an unapplied choice.


Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — Routing effects are keyed to the executing session, but tier changes and user-source notes use the default shared data directory. Consequently, a forged accepted answer could affect that session's selected provider and shared model-tier information used by other sessions sharing the directory. Cross-account or infrastructure-wide authority is not established by this path.

Security Findings and Attack Paths

inferred — The conditional attack path is a render-page or stale submission producing a valid answer, followed by automatic promotion to a user-source plan edit and session selection. The local consumer accepts this path without checking outstanding choices. The external host's result provenance and submission authorization remain unresolved, so this is not a verified end-to-end exploit.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — The answer boundary performs structural validation, not offered-value authorization: any nonempty model string with a recognized tier can reach setModel, which permits creating a new store entry. Execution subsequently rejects models absent from the catalog, but that check occurs after the plan write and user-source note.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

observed — Plan-file replacement is individually atomic, but answer settlement spans separate wall clearing, plan writing, note appending, pending-state recording, and later session selection. Tool-side application errors are ignored. Thus individual file integrity does not provide an atomic or recoverable end-to-end choice transition.

Hardening Proposals

proposed — Bind accepted answers to a specific outstanding session card and its offered values, and establish the host's user-submission guarantee. Resolve executable recovery targets before offering them, and distinguish successful application from an unapplied or interrupted choice rather than silently consuming it.

opencode.title: fix(ai): bound WebSocket inbound queue memory

nodes.bodyText:
No actionable comments were generated in the recent review.



Walkthrough



fromWebSocket now limits inbound buffering to 32 MiB and 4,096 messages. It fails the stream and closes an open socket with code 1009 when a limit is exceeded. Queue accounting decreases as messages are consumed. Tests cover ordering and limit boundaries.
Changes: WebSocket inbound buffering



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Inbound queue bounds and accounting  packages/ai/src/route/transport/websocket.ts, packages/ai/test/executor.test.ts, .jules/bolt.md
The receive path tracks queued bytes and messages, rejects overflow with buffer-overflow, and closes an open socket with code 1009. It releases accounting as messages are consumed. Tests check frame ordering, byte and message limits, and overflow behavior. The journal records these limits and actions.




Estimated code review effort: 2 (Simple) | ~12 minutes


Change: Bug fix

Sequence Diagram(s)

  
    
      sequenceDiagram
  participant WebSocket
  participant fromWebSocket
  participant MessageStream
  WebSocket->>fromWebSocket: Deliver inbound frame
  fromWebSocket->>fromWebSocket: Check limits and update queue counters
  alt Queue limit exceeded
    fromWebSocket->>MessageStream: Fail with buffer-overflow
    fromWebSocket->>WebSocket: Close with code 1009
  else Frame accepted
    fromWebSocket->>MessageStream: Queue frame
    MessageStream->>fromWebSocket: Consume frame and decrement counters
  end

    
  
  
    
  
    
    
    Loading

  


Possibly related issues

#2330: The issue describes unbounded growth in the inbound WebSocket queue. This change adds cumulative byte and message limits and releases accounting as messages are consumed.

Suggested reviewers: kitlangton, rekram1-node





Merge Risk:  Minimal · up to 56adb






This change bounds the memory a WebSocket connection can hold for pending inbound messages, and a connection that exceeds the limits now fails and closes instead of growing without limit. No concrete merge-blocking risk was found.





Security architecture risk:  Low · up to 56adb





The change limits a previously unbounded resource without expanding access or privileges. No introduced security defect was established. Large legitimate bursts now fail explicitly, while precise failure ordering and memory-release timing remain unverified.
Retained concerns
No architecture-level concerns identified.

Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — A peer able to send frames on an established connection can consume that connection's allowance and trigger its failure. The guard reduces the existing unbounded-retention exposure but is not a process-wide memory budget: multiple connections each have their own allowance, and transport-native buffers and downstream-held messages are outside this accounting.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — Connection establishment still uses the caller-provided URL and headers, and inbound data still enters through the existing socket message listener. The PR adds admission restrictions before downstream frame interpretation without adding a new peer-selection path, identity transition, or credential authority.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

observed — Overflow invokes queue failure and socket closure rather than immediate queue shutdown. Explicit connection cleanup removes listeners and invokes Queue.shutdown; the direct executor registers connection.close as its existing scope release action. Immediate reclamation and delivery of already-buffered frames cannot be established without the queue implementation's terminal-state semantics.

nodes.bodyText:
Closing per Drew's ruling (2026-11-07 23:02 CST):

there should be no such thing as a pool level verdict. a pool can't run out only models and providers run out.

This PR's direction — bench evidence stops counting toward the pool verdict once its gates re-judge clear — keeps the pool-level verdict mechanism itself. Under the ruling, that mechanism is abolished: eligibility is derived at decision time from per-leg state only (a leaf's own bench, its credential's gate, its provider's skip record and quota gate), no pool-level quota fact is stored or synthesized, and the pool-quota-exhausted exclusion reason is removed. openchamber.title: Probe successor gives up when its predecessor dies mid-exchange (#81 follow-up)

nodes.bodyText:
No actionable comments were generated in the recent review.



Walkthrough



The successor handoff probe now treats predecessor IPC disconnection before a verdict as a preflight failure. It clears both listeners when the exchange settles and uses the same settlement path for hello-send errors. Tests cover the gate and process behavior. Documentation names state.json and draining.json.
Changes: Handoff probe disconnect handling



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Probe settlement and validation  packages/web/server/lib/opencode/handoff-probe.js, packages/web/server/lib/opencode/handoff-probe.test.js, packages/web/server/lib/opencode/self-handoff-process.test.js, packages/web/server/lib/opencode/DOCUMENTATION.md
The probe handles predecessor disconnection as preflight-failed and removes both listeners when settled. Unit and process tests cover this behavior. The documentation identifies state.json and draining.json as preflight checks.




Estimated code review effort: 2 (Simple) | ~10 minutes


Change: Bug fix

Possibly related issues

Issue 2494 requests successor exit with preflight-failed when the IPC channel closes before the hello verdict. This change adds that disconnect handling and a process test.
Issue 81 describes a broader supervisor-driven upgrade handoff. This change covers the successor-side protocol probe, but not the full supervisor proposal.

Possibly related PRs

developing-today-forks/openchamber#2322: That PR maintains the state.json and draining.json pair that this PR now names in the documentation.

Suggested reviewers: btriapitsyn





Merge Risk:  Minimal · up to 5c280






A successor process now exits with a preflight failure when its predecessor dies before replying, instead of waiting indefinitely. The upgrade documentation now names the correct state files. The change is narrow and tested, with no remaining merge-blocking risk identified.





Security architecture risk:  Minimal · up to 5c280





The change makes an interrupted upgrade stop rather than wait indefinitely, without weakening the existing approval checks. No introduced or worsened architecture-level security, failure-containment, or ownership risk was established.
Retained concerns
No architecture-level concerns identified.

Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — The changed outcome is scoped to the local probe successor and its inherited listener copy. The change does not add a network entrypoint or expand the IPC peer's authority; it makes channel loss abort rather than authorize takeover.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — The successor still validates the inherited listener's host and port and the managed-state file versions before sending hello. Approval remains a message on the inherited process IPC channel; disconnection is handled only as failure, not as a replacement for approval.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

inferred — The fix is bounded to the verdict-wait window. Disconnect-listener registration still follows asynchronous preflight work, so the new listener alone does not cover a channel that closed earlier. This limitation existed at the comparison base and is not retained as an introduced or worsened concern.
observed — Existing startup can claim the recorded instance directory before the probe, so abort does not imply that no ownership metadata was touched. Subsequent preparation can reclaim that directory from a dead owner and excludes the claimed directory from abandoned-folder removal.

openchamber.title: Upgrade takeover for self-handoff: handoff protocol 2 (#81)

nodes.bodyText:
Caution
Review failed

The pull request is closed.





  Autofix · Keep fixing CodeRabbit findings and required CI, and resolving merge conflicts

Reviewed against the design of record on #81 (comment 6783127941), stages 2–4, at head 87a984451 (the one commit past 80dbbf5ab is a one-line test-fixture portability fix; re-verified after it). Approving — the implementation matches the design, and I re-ran the validation rather than taking the table on faith:
Re-run in a clean checkout of the PR head (Linux sandbox, bun install + vitest):

Focused unit suites (self-handoff, handoff-probe, lifecycle-handoff-probe, startup-pipeline-runtime, cli-args): 60 passed — matches the claimed count exactly.
Process matrix, new upgrade handoff across installs describe: 10 passed — upgrade with zero refused and zero failed client requests (the client loop counts any non-200 as failed, so this also covers the design §3 "hold, don't refuse" requirement empirically), downgrade refused then allowed, entry-invalid, silent successor, protocol-99 hello aborted, hang after go, exit after go, re-claim after a claiming successor hangs, unreadable state version, predecessor-too-old.
Pre-existing self-handoff across real processes block (the §6.4 one-phase regression): 17 passed.
Neighboring suites (lifecycle, lifecycle-handoff, listener-handoff, managed-process-claim, managed state + store, handoff-request, managed-config-file, agent-tool runtime, cli-startup, cli-control): 288 passed, 1 skipped, no failures.

Design points checked in the code, not just the tests: the probe gate runs in the startup pipeline immediately before listen; the single OPENCHAMBER_HANDOFF_TIMEOUT_MS timer budgets hello + go + ready; a failed preflight travels as an abort so the predecessor names preflight-failed instead of a bare exit; the re-claim is guarded to the failed successor, the predecessor itself, or a dead owner (unit + process tests both pin the "another live server's child is left alone" case), so no interleaving leaves two owners or a dead one; predecessor-too-old fires exactly when the instance file lacks handoffProtocol, before any request file is written.
Two non-blocking notes (follow-ups, not merge conditions):

handoff-probe.js: the gate's verdict promise has no successor-side timeout or IPC disconnect handling. If the predecessor dies after spawning the successor but before answering the hello, the successor waits indefinitely, holding its fd 3 copy — the socket stays open, requests queue in the backlog, and the port stays wedged until the successor is killed by hand. No session or data loss (OpenCode is untouched and the predecessor's death is itself the incident), and the design budgets the sequence on the predecessor side only, so this is outside the §6 matrix — but an exit-on-disconnect guard plus a process test would close it cheaply.
DOCUMENTATION.md, upgrade-takeover bullet: it says the successor checks the version fields of state.json and store.json; the probe (checkStateVersions) actually checks state.json and draining.json — the v1 pair the design §3 names. Worth a one-word doc fix so the doc doesn't send a reader to the wrong file.

Merging on the strength of the above. After this lands, the only open acceptance item on #81 is design §6 item 5 — the real-systemd MainPID check, which is manual/CI-optional by design.

Medium · reliability · inferred: Save ordering is scoped to a writer instance rather than the session’s outstanding edits. inferred — A policy-integrity failure needs no new external caller: starting from models A, B, and C, remove A, navigate away and back before the save settles, then remove B. The recreated writer can build its replacement from the old saved policy and submit A and C, restoring A. An older writer can also clear the newer writer’s displayed pending state because cleanup checks sessionId but not writer identity. observed — The shared picker filters hidden models from provider, favorite, and recent rows. Selection still invokes the caller’s handler rather than granting the list persistence authority. observed — Within one writer, failed writes are reported, later queued writes continue, and pending state clears when the queue drains. They do not establish ordering across recreated writers.

proposed — Keep one pending-policy owner and serialization queue for each session/directory identity until its outstanding work drains, independent of navigation. Associate pending-state cleanup with that owner’s generation so an older writer cannot clear newer work.

Bootstrap installs the /api guard before feature-route registration on the same app. The guard delegates tunnel and unknown-public requests to tunnel-session enforcement and other requests to the UI authentication controller; delete is not among its listed exemptions. These limitations predate the PR; the inspected change does not establish that they became more exposed.

proposed — If concurrent untrusted filesystem writers are part of the threat model, consider directory-identity-bound deletion or equivalent isolation rather than treating canonical path-string checks as a race-proof guarantee.

Merge Risk:  Low · up to 4fda4






Replacing AGENTS.md is now atomic and a failed replacement preserves the old file. However, a restricted AGENTS.md, for example mode 0600, can become world-readable (0644 under umask 0022) after it is saved through this endpoint. The practical exposure is small and the fix is two lines. It is worth fixing before or soon after merge.





Security architecture risk:  Low · up to 4fda4





Atomic replacement protects saved content, but saving an existing private AGENTS.md can reset its permissions and expose the prompt to additional local users. Exposure depends on process defaults and directory access.
Retained concerns

Low · security · inferred: Replacing AGENTS.md with a newly created staging inode discards its existing restrictive permissions. An existing 0600 file can become 0644 under umask 022, allowing other local users who can traverse the parent directories to read previously private behavior content after a legitimate save. The staging content is subject to those defaults before commit as well. The previous direct write preserved the existing file's mode; private directories and restrictive process defaults limit this exposure.


Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — The identified permission regression is bounded to AGENTS.md and its staging copies under the server-selected global configuration directory. Exploiting the additional read exposure requires local filesystem access and traversable parent directories; it does not require the reader to invoke the HTTP endpoint. Exposure of any particular sensitive content or deployed account was not established.

Security Findings and Attack Paths

inferred — A legitimate save can change an existing file-level access restriction: the handler creates the staging file with filesystem defaults and promotes that inode without copying the old mode. A less-privileged local reader may then gain access to prompt content that the previous in-place write would have kept restricted. This consequence is conditional on the effective umask and directory permissions.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — Request content is written to a fixed AGENTS.md path derived from server environment configuration, not a request-supplied filename. The PR changes the filesystem mutation mechanism, not route registration or authentication middleware. Replacing the destination symlink also avoids writing the submitted content through that symlink to its target.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

inferred — Same-directory rename removes the previous truncate-and-write visibility window, so normal readers see the old or complete new file. Cleanup is best-effort for caught errors: a process termination before rename bypasses the catch and can leave staged content, while unlink errors are ignored. This does not establish crash durability or guaranteed removal of every staging copy.

Hardening Proposals

proposed — Define an explicit access-policy invariant for staged and committed AGENTS.md content, preserving existing restrictions during replacement rather than relying solely on process defaults. Validate replacement of a restrictive existing file under a more permissive umask.

Window geometry saving is unchanged in ordinary use. In a narrow overlap, where an older save is still pending while a newer one is scheduled, the newer geometry may not be saved until the next window move or close. A one-line fix (use a unique token per schedule) and a regression test would close this before merge.

If revision 1 remains pending while revision 2 completes through the Quake-mode no-op path, cleanup removes revision 2. The next schedule restarts at revision 1, allowing the original completion to delete its revision. The newer timer then skips its save and retains its timer-map entry. The settings queue does not prevent this no-op completion from overtaking an earlier write.

The new finally block performs revision cleanup but does not introduce the rejection-containment behavior. The settings-mutation queue separately preserves its ability to process later mutations after rejection.

Security architecture risk:  Moderate · up to 71fdd





Rotation is opt-in and includes meaningful safeguards. However, an uncertain switch outcome can allow additional sessions to move without the intended pacing or complete history, weakening failure containment and recovery.
Retained concerns

Medium · reliability · inferred: An uncertain switch outcome does not reserve the pool's move interval or trigger reconciliation. The timeout wrapper races the mutation without cancelling its underlying promise, and every switch error backs off only that session before trying another. Only acknowledged successes enter move history and pacing state. If OpenCode applies a switch but its response is lost or delayed, another session can move in the same interval while the first move remains unrecorded. Because each move removes pool failover, this is a failure-containment and recovery gap introduced by making rotation live, not merely a history-display issue. The production client supplies an abort signal, but no server-side cancellation or rollback guarantee was established.

Security Blast Radius

inferred — Enablement applies across eligible pools processed by this server instance, potentially spanning session project directories. The settings caller cannot directly supply session IDs, destination addresses, or credentials: sessions come from telemetry and destinations from configuration.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

That guard selects tunnel-session enforcement for tunnel or unknown-public traffic and otherwise delegates to the configured UI authentication policy. These enforcement files are unchanged by the PR; the new route does not establish a separate authentication bypass.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

inferred — The overlap guard, session rereads, and per-session backoff contain acknowledged failures within one process. They do not reconcile uncertain mutation outcomes, so the recorded move history can diverge from externally applied session state and cannot reliably account for every session that lost pool failover.

Hardening Proposals

proposed — Distinguish definite rejection from an uncertain switch outcome. For uncertain outcomes, reserve the pool's move interval, stop further moves in that pool, and reconcile session state before resuming. Track pending and reconciled outcomes so delayed application remains visible; validate recovery against a switch that applies but never returns a successful response.

nodes.bodyText:
Thanks for the PR. This one is large (XL, about 676 changed lines after excluding tests, lockfiles, translation catalogs and evidence images), so I'm parking it with needs-discussion rather than reviewing it as-is.
A change this size almost always carries a product decision, and that's easier to settle in words than inside a diff. Even when it doesn't change where the product is going, this many touched files changes how it behaves in places nobody asked about, so the question is still whether we want this change at all, and in this shape. Please open an Ideas discussion describing what changes for the user and why, then add the link to this PR's description. The label comes off on the next push or edit.
If the diff is mostly mechanical (generated files, a rename that touched everything), say so here and the maintainer will take a look anyway. Splitting off the bug fixes into their own PRs also works: those get reviewed straight away.
Nothing closes automatically because of this label. The usual stale rule still applies: 28 days without activity marks the PR stale, 7 more days closes it.

Walkthrough



This pull request adds persistent server-side goal-spec jobs and client support to create, review, edit, and send generated specs. It adds job synchronization, composer handoff, a chat card, and tests for server and UI behavior.
Changes: Goal-spec job flow



Layer / File(s)
Summary




Server job runtime and routes  packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/spec-jobs.js, packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/spec-jobs.test.js
The server adds persistent job state, spec writing, send and claim operations, lifecycle handling, and HTTP routes. Tests cover writing, delivery, recovery, claims, and routes.


Client job state and synchronization  packages/ui/src/stores/goalSpecJobStore.ts, packages/ui/src/lib/openchamberEvents.ts, packages/ui/src/sync/goal-spec-job-sync.ts, packages/ui/src/stores/goalSpecJobStore.test.ts, packages/ui/src/lib/openchamberEvents.test.ts
The client validates and tracks jobs, reconciles snapshots and events by revision, and resynchronizes on stream readiness. Tests cover hydration, updates, mutations, and event dispatch.

The client sends claimed messages and restores returned text, attachments, and context to the matching composer. Send options support a goal-arm override and an optimistic message-ID callback.

The card presents job status, writer and length-limit controls, and actions to edit, retry, or send. The model selector supports a disabled state, and the UI adds localized messages and tests for card choices and sent-job status.

Possibly related issues

#1573: The issue asks to port the goal-spec job implementation, and this pull request adds the named server runtime and client job, send, and edit modules.


Suggested reviewers: btriapitsyn, dezren39





Merge Risk:  High · up to 0762f






The goal-spec job flow has open correctness gaps around delivery durability, duplicate or premature sends, runtime switching, and composer restoration. Users could see prompts sent early or twice, or messages that cannot be recovered after Back to edit. It is not safe to merge until the delivery and settlement races are fixed and the production wiring is confirmed.





Security architecture risk:  Low · up to 0762f





Replacement recovery can revive an outdated request, and capacity handling can discard an unsent request. These affect message ownership and recovery. Current exposure is limited because the new server flow is not connected to the inspected production routing.
Retained concerns

Medium · reliability · inferred: A failed replacement unconditionally restores its predecessor without checking whether another replacement now owns the session. If replacement A supersedes the original job, replacement B supersedes A, and A's save fails, A's recovery can leave both B and the original job active. Reopening also restarts writing or waiting work, allowing superseded work to send again when automatic delivery is enabled. Serialized file writes do not serialize this recovery decision. This defect is in the new runtime; production activation is not established.
Medium · reliability · observed: At the runtime-wide 50-job limit, capacity eviction protects active delivery but not writing, review, or queued waiting jobs. It cancels the oldest eligible open job without returning its message to a composer. Eviction occurs before the incoming job is saved, and creation failure does not restore that evicted job. Consequently, creating work for one session can discard another session's unsent message even when the new creation fails. Settled jobs are evicted first, which limits but does not eliminate this failure-containment defect.


Security review details



Security Blast Radius

inferred — If activated, the runtime holds pending work across sessions within one server instance and dispatches using injected OpenCode credentials. Delivery can change a session's model and agent, create its goal, insert synthetic instructions, and submit a prompt. The observed defects affect pending-work ownership within that runtime; cross-tenant reachability or additional downstream privileges are not established.

Trust Boundaries and Controls

observed — Client claim/send handling captures the originating runtime and rejects a claim answered after switching away. Store updates reject other-runtime and older-revision responses; runtime reset clears jobs and held claims. Composer restores require matching runtime, directory, and session identity rather than session ID alone.

Resilience and Maintainability Implications

observed — Active delivery and waiting guards prevent ordinary repeated send/claim requests from taking concurrent ownership. Settlement must match an active composer's claim; uncertain or expired delivery returns to review. These controls limit accidental repeated execution but do not repair replacement rollback or capacity eviction.
